title: Core Protocol for Serial Imaging of Fluorescently-Labeled Mouse Brain
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be2ejgbe
materials: Vibratome blade (Accutek Blades Microkeratome Blade part 89-0034-0000)
Mai Tai Laser Head (on Newport air table)
PC connected to laser running MaiTai software (Spectra Physics Mai Tai 0454-8260).
Network attached storage arrays (one on each system)
PF0315 TissueCyte Specimen Embedding - Acrylamide co-embedding
RP0197 Phosphate Buffer with 0.1% Sodium Azide
EQ0067 TissueCyte Installation and Alignment Guide
Start up the Channel 1 PC and open the Orchestrator software from its desktop icon.
Note: with the TissueVision software, do not press buttons repeatedly as this causes the system to crash. Press a button and wait for the action to be completed prior to pressing the button again.
Figure 8: Mai Tai laser power switches

steps.title: Safety check and laser power‑up
steps.instruction: Wear laser safety goggles (OD > 5 at 925 nm), keep laser shuttered and PMTs off before opening the TissueCyte doors; verify air‑table pressure is ~40 psi (contact Engineering if it oscillates); turn on the chiller (set to 21 °C) and, if temperature is off‑spec, contact Engineering for Chlor‑T; turn on the Mai Tai power supply (orange switch) and wait 2 min, then turn the key ON (90° clockwise) to start laser initialization; at 65 % warm‑up select the “_20XW1.00ZEI” template (press DOWN); wait ~40 min for 100 % warm‑up; double‑click the Spectra‑Physics Mai Tai software and click OK; when status shows “Ready to turn on”, hold the ON button 3 s until the EMISSION light turns on; set wavelength to 925 nm (slider adjusts ~30 s); open the laser shutter (hold SHUTTER 3 s) and turn off overhead room lights.

steps.title: Prepare Vibratome and blade
steps.instruction: Remove the Vibratome arm from inside the TissueCyte using a 3/32″ hex key; loosen the 0.05″ screws on the back, remove the used blade and dispose of it in a sharps container; place the new blade in the Vibratome; reinstall the arm, tighten evenly so it is parallel with the block face.

steps.title: Launch software and connect hardware
steps.instruction: Open the Vivace client on PC2, go to the Services tab and click “Connect All” to initialize the x, y, z stages, Vibratome and imaging module; once all checkboxes turn green, click Client to launch; on the slave system click “Reference Stage”.

steps.title: Register sample and mount slide
steps.instruction: In Orchestrator’s Protocol tab highlight the Sample ID bar, scan the slide barcode with the handheld scanner and confirm the number populates; enter the 5‑digit specimen number in the Description field; place the barcoded slide on the raised metal platform in the bath with the brain top facing the TissueCyte doors and the barcode end on the left; use a T‑square ruler and bath side screws to center the specimen midline parallel to the bath sides.

steps.title: Fill and load bath
steps.instruction: Fill the bath with 50 mM phosphate buffer containing 0.1 % sodium azide (SOP RP0197) until the solution is midway up the bath cover, adding slowly to avoid bubbles and displacing any bubbles under the slide with a transfer pipette; carefully load the bath into the microscope, push it back to its limit and rotate the left‑side screw to secure it.

steps.title: Initial z‑axis positioning and trim sections
steps.instruction: In Orchestrator’s Imaging tab use Stage Control to raise the z‑axis in <1000 µm increments until the top of the agarose block is roughly level with the Vibratome blade; click “Slice” to cut a 100 µm section—if the blade is still above the block, raise the stage 100‑200 µm and slice again; after the first cut, cut two additional sections without moving the z‑stage (total of three) to establish a flat cutting plane.

steps.title: Trim brainstem to cerebellum
steps.instruction: Continue slicing through the brainstem until the edge of the cerebellum becomes visible; the final trim section should contain both brainstem and a small piece of cerebellum.

steps.title: Calibrate laser power and PMTs
steps.instruction: Check laser power at the objective and adjust the V2 setting in Vivace on the Channel 1 PC by 0.05 steps to reach the required power (TC0 only); open the internal TissueCyte shutter (change from “Automatic” to “Open”, TC0 only); with both shutters open, move the stage forward in 1000 µm steps until the brainstem is illuminated; close the internal TissueCyte shutter (set back to “Automatic”); turn on the PMTs by enabling the voltage supply (or opening the GUI) and set the voltage to 600‑650 V (recommended 600, 625, 650 V); take a 2D snapshot via Orchestrator and set Image Display from “Auto Max/Min” to “Manual”.

steps.title: Find sample top and set imaging depth
steps.instruction: Use the piezo controller to raise the objective up to 400 µm (twist dial clockwise to move down, counter‑clockwise to move up) and locate the top surface of the sample; record the piezo value, then move 50 µm deeper; move to an area showing only brainstem tissue and ensure the mean image intensity is ≥250 (abort if <200); if intensity is low, increase PMT voltage up to 650 V; if intensity is >600, decrease voltage to 600 V.

steps.title: Center specimen in field of view
steps.instruction: Find the right and left edges by moving the stage in 1000 µm increments, then move to the L/R centre; find front and back edges by moving in 500 µm increments, then move to the F/B centre; align the brain’s central canal at the middle‑right edge of the Channel 1 image (or, if the canal is absent, align the midline 100 µm past the middle‑left edge); once centred, move the stage 5.5 mm (5500 µm) back and 5.8 mm (5800 µm) right; set the piezo to 75‑100 µm below the recorded top surface.

steps.title: Configure and start mosaic acquisition
steps.instruction: Confirm that the image‑storage drive letter is identical on both Master and Slave PCs; in Orchestrator’s Protocol tab open the Mosaic Settings panel and enter the required image parameters; click “Update settings” and verify that Vivace mirrors these settings; click “3D mosaic” to begin imaging of the entire brain (≈18 h); keep overhead lights off and keep the sliding door closed for the duration of the run.

steps.title: Shutdown and collect sections
steps.instruction: After the mosaic finishes (Channel 1 PC shows “Completed 3D mosaic”), turn off the PMT power supply and open the TissueCyte doors; using the Z‑stage control in the Imaging tab, lower the stage ≈35 mm so the bath is beneath the Vibratome blade; loosen the bath screw and carefully remove the bath; place a nylon mesh strainer over a 1000 ml beaker in the sink and pour the buffer plus floating sections through the strainer; rinse repeatedly to ensure all sections are removed, using a small paintbrush for any remaining pieces; transfer the sections from the mesh into the original conical tube labeled with specimen and project information, cap, label with the operating week, and parafilm around cap and tube; store the tube at 4 °C protected from direct light.

steps.title: Clean equipment and record data
steps.instruction: Clean the empty bath by flushing with tap water followed by deionized water and air‑dry (no soap); enter the TissueCyte run information into the Laboratory Information Management System; ensure laser safety goggles (OD > 5 at 925 nm) are available for future runs; perform routine system maintenance as described in SOP EQ0063.
